clue.text: One who surely won't follow doggedly?

definitions.text: One who surely won't follow doggedly?

parts.words: One who surely won't follow doggedly?
parts.note: a cat is no dog, so it would hardly follow doggedly, yet this kind of cat is exactly a follower who imitates others

explanation.surface: A remark about someone who refuses to tag along behind like a loyal hound.
explanation.definitionFit: An imitator who copies what others do is the person described, punning on cat versus dog.

clue.text: Character of a Shakespeare play that's gathering dust?

definitions.meaning: one of Titania's fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream bears this name
the spider's thread found in neglected corners collects dust

explanation.surface: A question about a Shakespearean role that has been sitting neglected on the shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a fairy in the Dream and the dusty thread a spider spins in old corners.

clue.text: Prudent giving it into keeping of constabulary, for the most part

indicators.note: put into the keeping of something means placed inside it
only most of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: the constabulary is the police force
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sensible person hands something over to the police to look after.
explanation.definitionFit: Politic is an adjective meaning shrewd and sensible in one's actions, a synonym of prudent.

clue.text: Ravel score with end beginning to climax: this heard?

definitions.text: Ravel score with end beginning to climax: this heard?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
to ravel is to tangle, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as anagram fodder
taken as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Ravel's famous Bolero builds steadily to a climax, and that is what you hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravel' is the composer in the surface but the anagram signal in the wordplay. His Bolero is the classic example of the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradual swelling of volume rising to a peak is exactly what Ravel's Bolero famously delivers.

clue.text: What may show reduced waist measurement thanks to exercise?

definitions.text: What may show reduced waist measurement thanks to exercise?

parts.words: What may show reduced waist measurement thanks to exercise?
parts.note: the dieter's measuring strip wrapped round the middle reveals the smaller girth after workouts

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether their workouts have trimmed their middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape measure is the flexible strip used to measure a waistline.

clue.text: Here's us involved in sitting mainly for French painter

indicators.note: being involved in something means being wrapped up inside it
mainly means most of it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: sitting for an artist is posing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims a part in a portrait session for a French artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicolas Poussin was a seventeenth-century French classical painter.

clue.text: Public relations officer with Tube regularly disowns numbers coming off line

parts.note: PRO is the standard abbreviation for a public relations officer
a duct is a tube or channel

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A PR man on the London Underground denies responsibility for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the second, fourth and sixth letters of 'disowns', I, O, N. 'Tube' looks like the London Underground but is just a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Output is the quantity of goods emerging from a production line.

clue.text: One holds female not suitable

indicators.note: one word holds another inside it

parts.note: a unit is a single one

explanation.surface: A single person keeps hold of a woman who is not right for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfit is an adjective meaning unsuitable or not good enough for a purpose.

clue.text: Records turning up leading to impulse to spend extravagantly

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: LPs are long-playing records
an urge is a sudden impulse

explanation.surface: Finding old vinyl prompts a sudden desire to go on a spending spree.
explanation.definitionFit: To splurge is to spend money freely and lavishly on a treat.

clue.text: At this juncture, say, a Down may be anagrammed

indicators.note: the clue openly says the letters can be rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A setter jokes that a Down clue can be scrambled at this point in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowadays means in the present age, at this point in time.

clue.text: Slug repellent?

parts.note: a slug is also a bullet, and something that repels bullets resists gunfire

explanation.surface: A gardener's product for keeping slimy pests off the lettuces.
explanation.definitionFit: Armour that stops a bullet repels a slug in its firearms sense.

clue.text: Cow's call is only half the length of a bull's

indicators.text: is only half the length of
indicators.note: keeping only half the length of a six-letter word drops its first three letters

parts.note: a bull's call is a bellow

explanation.surface: A comparison of a cow's moo with a bull's roar.
explanation.walkthrough: BELLOW is six letters; half its length, the last three, is the cow's own call.
explanation.definitionFit: A low is the mooing sound a cow makes.

clue.text: Person bound to learn to sacrifice pawn and rook to offer temptation

indicators.note: to sacrifice pieces in chess is to give them up, so these letters are removed

parts.note: a prentice, short for apprentice, is someone bound by indenture to learn a trade
P is the chess notation for pawn
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A young chess student is taught to give up pieces as a lure for the opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: PRENTICE is an old short form of apprentice. Chess pieces in the surface are just the letters P and R.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure someone by offering something tempting.

clue.text: Something very popular with four of our editors — like some pearls

parts.note: a cult is something enjoying a devoted popular following

indicators.note: four letters are taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something that is a hit with several of the newspaper's editors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four of' takes URED from inside 'our editors'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cultured pearls are grown in farmed oysters rather than found wild.

clue.text: Rats aren't socially acceptable running around here?

indicators.note: letters running around are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder
U stands for upper-class, hence socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A diner is assured that no rodents scamper around on these premises.
explanation.walkthrough: U meaning upper-class or socially acceptable is an old British convention. 'Here' is the definition: the place where rats are unwelcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A dining establishment is the place pointed to, where scurrying rats would never be tolerated.

clue.text: Making changes to force nice Tony to offer sweet things

indicators.note: changes to the letters signal that they are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone tinkers to make a pleasant man called Tony hand out sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: Confectionery is the collective word for sweets and candies.

clue.text: Start with one soldier, about to get decorated

indicators.note: one word placed about others goes round them

parts.note: ornate means richly decorated
I is the Roman numeral for one
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is about to receive a medal and begins his career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'soon going to', but 'about' is the container signal and 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to begin or come into being, a verb meaning to start.

clue.text: Sign of Corinthians gaining power in the Christian church

indicators.note: 'in' says the abbreviations for the epistle and for power are set inside the word for the church

parts.note: Sion, a variant of Zion, is used for the Christian church as the heavenly city
Cor is the abbreviation for the epistle Corinthians
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A passage from St Paul's letter to the Corinthians grows in influence in the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: COR gaining P gives CORP, placed in SION.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scorpion is the zodiac sign also called Scorpio.

clue.text: One who arranges his own supply when it comes to parts?

definitions.text: One who arranges his own supply when it comes to parts?

parts.words: One who arranges his own supply when it comes to parts?
parts.note: a supple performer twists his own body parts into strange arrangements, punning on supply and supple

explanation.surface: A man who sorts out his own spare parts deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus performer who bends and twists their limbs into extraordinary positions is meant.

clue.text: Flummox — might this be its equivalent?

definitions.text: Flummox — might this be its equivalent?

parts.words: Flummox — might this be its equivalent?
parts.note: a word for baffle that read as not-plus would mean minus, the opposite of plus

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a word could serve as a synonym for bewilder.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to perplex or bewilder them so they do not know what to do.

clue.text: Joint winning team

definitions.meaning: a cut of beef from the outer thigh, used as a roasting joint
the side that comes out on top

explanation.surface: A two-word phrase suggesting a shared victorious squad.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a lean cut of beef for roasting and, split up, the leading side.

clue.text: Young bird not going far from its pen

definitions.text: Young bird not going far from its pen

parts.words: Young bird not going far from its pen
parts.note: a pen is a female swan, and her baby stays close to her rather than to a farmyard enclosure

explanation.surface: A chick that won't wander far from its coop.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby swan stays near its mother, the female swan called a pen.

clue.text: What fight manager might do to get small aircraft

definitions.meaning: a boxing promoter would organise a contest in the ring
a light plane used for short trips

explanation.surface: A boxing promoter tries to get hold of a little plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Split, it describes running a boxing match; whole, it names a small light vehicle or aircraft.

clue.text: Cheese set without new preservative

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A cheese is set aside without anything fresh to keep it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' in the old sense of 'outside' puts BRIE round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Salty water is used for pickling and preserving food.

clue.text: Just succeeded with hint

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded
to imply is to hint

explanation.surface: Someone managed it merely by dropping a suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: Simply and just are adverbs both meaning merely or only.

clue.text: Daughter is caught by something moving in the spine

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A girl is taken aback by something stirring in her back.
explanation.definitionFit: Intervertebral cartilage pads sit between the vertebrae and can slip out of place.

clue.text: What some bacillus might make you

definitions.text: What some bacillus might make you

indicators.note: some of a word means only part of its letters are used

explanation.surface: A warning that a bacterium could do you harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Infection by a bacterium can make a person sick.

clue.text: Fancy island country being led by wise men

indicators.note: being led by means coming after, so the wise men go in front of the country

parts.note: the Magi are the wise men of the Nativity
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: An elaborate island state ruled by sages.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy as a noun means the creative faculty of the mind, a synonym for imagination.

clue.text: North America's local coin coming into circulation?

parts.note: NA is the abbreviation for North America, plus the possessive S
the cent is the coin used locally in North America

explanation.surface: A North American coin begins to be passed around.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into existence, here fancifully put as entering circulation like a coin.

clue.text: Being kind and gentle when learner gets in fix

indicators.note: one item gets in another, going inside it

parts.note: cement is used to fix things firmly together
L is the learner plate abbreviation

explanation.surface: A novice is gentle when stuck in a difficult situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' reads as a predicament but is CEMENT; 'gets in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement means merciful and mild, as in clement weather or a clement judge.
